title: GIANT CS2CT Signal Sifter tutorial
bodyHtml:
In the View Data section:
1. Set phenotype (e.g. BMI_GIANT)
2. Set ancestry (e.g. Mixed)
3. Set annotation (e.g. accessible_chromatin)
4. Set tissue (e.g. central nervous system)
5. Click Search


 

In the dropdown menus in the CS2CT by annotation and tissue section:
6. Set Source on the next tab to credible_set to limit credible sets to the SNPs provided by GIANT (the others are precalculated credible sets from the portal)


NOTE: If you forget to do this you may need to Reset and start over
 

7. Set any filters for PPO, entropy (or specify a CS if you know the ID).
This gives you a PPO vs entropy graph (clicking the dots provides credible set regions and a biosample that is involved in the overlap, along with PPO and entropy scores).


 

There are options to display entropy, entropy out, or entropy in. It also gives you a table of the credible sets.


 

The table can be sorted by clicking on the columns, e.g. entropy out is a good place to start.


 

In addition to filtering by Entropy or PPO, or specific CS ID, you can also filter by chromosome or biosample.


NOTE: clicking “view” only shows a couple of additional tables of information for that credible set – this is not the next step. 

Instead,
Once you have a credible set of interest:
1. Mouse over “Load variants” and click on Set CS ID & Region. This will produce a table of the credible set you’ve selected. You may want to star the row to have the lead SNP stared in the variants in the searching region.


 

2. You can star/unstar variants individually in the credible set clicking the star icon, and can star/unstar all of them by mousing over the star at the header row of the table.


 

3. The other tab allows you to see other credible sets in the region, with some minimal information about these; we have not done a lot with this tab.


 

4. Below the variant table will be a locuszoom-style figure and below that a table, both containing all variants in the credible set region +/- 200 kb. The figure is supposed to be centered on the lead variant from the CS (this did not appear to be true in Joel’s test run). The stared lead SNP will appear on the plot. Dotted lines appear on the position of the stared lead SNP on the plot and genes track.


 

5. If you starred variant(s) these will have a star-shaped icon and a dashed line indicating their position.
6. You can filter and sort this figure and table as well, and zoom in and out and pan (within the region defined by the widest zoom).

 

7. If you decide this is not a credible set you want to look at further, you can go back to the credible set table above and “load variants”/”Set CS ID & Region” for a new credible set and start over. Or you can click Reset near the top and start from scratch.
8. If you want to look at overlap with annotations across biosamples from the tissue, you can scroll down and see overlap with annotations in different biosamples) the dashed line(s) are still the starred variant(s).


 

9. You can display as many or as few biosamples as you want using the drop down menu, and also filter on which annotations are displayed, even down to a specific dataset. 


 

10. By clicking on the tab that says annotated regions – other tissues you can see the same overlap information but this time with annotations for biosamples from other tissues (each row is the union of annotations from biosamples in that tissue)

To look specifically at a biosample within a tissue, especially if you the number of rows in the variant table in the CS2CT by annotation + tissue section was capped at 10000 rows:
1. In the table within the CS2CT by annotation + tissue section, find a credible set with the biosample you are interested in (filter in the drop down menu if needed)
2. Mouse over “Load data” and click “Set annotation, tissue + biosample”


 

3. This will generate a new section “CS2CT by annotation + tissue + biosample” that works the same way as the CS2CT by annotation +tissue” section.
Then scroll to the bottom by update summary, then click annotations in region as well and there should be a table listing SNPs that overlap annotations with tissue in region (but some biosamples may not be loaded)
